claim: Axis Intelligence Research computes an implied US iPhone replacement cycle of 2.84 years for the twelve months ending September 2025, derived from CIRP's published retirement-age bucket midpoints, and disputes the widely-repeated 4+ year replacement-age figure as unsupported by any locatable published source.
stance_target: iPhone replacement cycle has lengthened to ~3.7-3.84 years (the batch's stated consensus prior)
scope_conditions: US iPhone buyers, twelve months to September 2025, derived metric
quoted_support: According to Axis Intelligence Research, the implied US iPhone replacement cycle stands at 2.8 years — materially shorter than the four-year-plus figure widely repeated in technology coverage, including in an earlier version of this page... Figures above four years that circulate widely are not supported by any published source we could locate.

claim: CIRP's retirement-age distribution shows the share of US iPhone buyers replacing a device 3+ years old rose from 24% (12 months to Sept 2020) to 42% (12 months to Sept 2025), then eased to 39% (quarter ending March 2026).
stance_target: structural lengthening of replacement cycle over a 5-year horizon, with a possible recent plateau
quoted_support: The direction is unambiguous and the magnitude is large: the share of buyers retiring a device three years or older rose from 24% to 42% in five years.

claim: CIRP's own framing for the March 2026 quarter describes the replacement-age distribution as bimodal: a shrinking middle two-to-three-year cohort, with growth at both ends -- very-long holders (4-5 years) and short-cycle carrier-lease buyers (12-18 months) -- meaning a single average replacement age describes almost nobody.
stance_target: usefulness of a single 'average replacement age' statistic for modeling upgrade revenue
quoted_support: The average is becoming a statistic that describes almost nobody. That matters for anyone modelling upgrade revenue, because the two groups respond to completely different levers.

claim: Apple reported $196.5 billion in iPhone net sales across the first nine months of fiscal 2026, up 22.4% year over year, including $54,252 million in the quarter ended June 27, 2026 (+21.7% YoY) per Apple's 10-Q; full fiscal 2025 iPhone net sales were $209,586 million.
stance_target: iPhone revenue trajectory (units x ASP effect)
quoted_support: Apple reported $196.5 billion in iPhone net sales across the first nine months of fiscal 2026, up 22.4% year over year... $54,252 million in the quarter ended June 27, 2026.

claim: iPhone's share of Apple's total revenue has fallen for three consecutive fiscal years (52.33% FY2023, 51.45% FY2024, 50.36% FY2025), but the June-quarter concentration ROSE from 47.41% (FY2025) to 49.58% (FY2026), reversing the annual dilution trend at the quarterly level.
stance_target: extent of Apple's revenue diversification away from iPhone dependency
scope_conditions: Apple SEC 10-K annual and quarterly filings, FY2023-FY2026
quoted_support: On an annual basis the ratio has fallen for three consecutive years, driven by Services growth rather than iPhone weakness. But the quarterly series tells a different story that the annual trend obscures: concentration in the June quarter rose from 47.41% in fiscal 2025 to 49.58% in fiscal 2026.

claim: IDC forecasts worldwide smartphone shipments will fall 13.9% in 2026 to approximately 1.09 billion units (the steepest annual contraction on record), driven by a memory/DRAM component shortage pushing average selling prices to a record $550, while iOS declines only 5.2% and reaches a record 22% annual share.
stance_target: ASP increases and share gains can offset unit stagnation/decline for Apple even as the broader market contracts
scope_conditions: IDC Worldwide Quarterly Mobile Phone Tracker, 2026 forecast
quoted_support: IDC forecasts a 13.9% decline to roughly 1.09 billion units, the steepest annual contraction on record, driven by a memory component shortage that is raising bill-of-materials costs and forcing price increases. Average selling prices are forecast to reach a record $550... IDC forecasts iOS will decline 5.2% in 2026 against a 20% Android decline, and reach a record 22% annual share.

claim: Apple left iPhone, Apple Watch and AirPods prices unchanged in its June 25, 2026 price increase, which raised US list prices across Mac, iPad, HomePod, Apple TV and Vision Pro citing memory costs.
stance_target: Apple's pricing strategy amid industry-wide memory cost shocks
quoted_support: On June 25, 2026, Apple raised US list prices across Mac, iPad, HomePod, Apple TV and Vision Pro, citing memory costs. iPhone, Apple Watch and AirPods prices were left unchanged.

claim: CIRP put iPhone platform loyalty at 87% for the March 2026 quarter, with 12% of new iPhone buyers switching from Android; Apple's installed base exceeded 2.5 billion active devices as of the quarter ended December 27, 2025 (not broken out by product).
stance_target: a lengthening hardware replacement cycle is a tailwind for services/installed-base monetization even if it compresses hardware unit volume
scope_conditions: CIRP US panel and Apple corporate disclosure
quoted_support: CIRP put iPhone platform loyalty at 87% in the March 2026 quarter, with 12% of new iPhone buyers arriving from Android... Apple stated an installed base of more than 2.5 billion active devices as of the quarter ended December 27, 2025.
